_what: Joining a browser extension to a program on this computer through the browser's own native-messaging manifest (computer/native-messaging.mjs). `browsers` are rows: where that browser looks for manifests (`folder`, under the home folder), and which key names the extensions it allows (`allow_key`: Chrome-family `allowed_origins` takes chrome-extension://<id>/ addresses, Firefox `allowed_extensions` takes ids). A new browser is a new row. A manifest's `name` must match `name_pattern`. `bridge` is the program the browser starts (computer/browser-bridge.mjs): its manifest `name`, the `launcher` file it writes, and `tools`, the only tool ids a browser extension may have this Mac run (none by default).

words.bad_name: {name} is not a valid native host name (lower case words joined by dots, like com.example.host).
words.bad_path: The host program must be an absolute path to a file that exists.
words.no_extensions: Name at least one extension that may talk to this host.
words.unknown_browser: There is no browser named {browser} in this list.
words.refused_foreign: {file} was not written by this program, so it was left as it is.

words.not_allowed: This Mac does not run {tool} for a browser extension.
words.foreign_launcher: There is already a file at {path} that this Mac did not write, so it was left as it is.
